title: Kac Moody Algebras from Generalized Cartan Matrices

items.title: Generalized cartan matrix
items.statement: Definition: $A=(a_{ij})$ has $a_{ii}=2$, $a_{ij}\in\mathbb Z_{\le0}$ for $i\ne j$, and $a_{ij}=0$ iff $a_{ji}=0$.
items.strategy: Fix a nonempty finite index set {1,...,n} and integer entries; all diagonal entries are 2, off-diagonal entries nonpositive, and the zero pattern is symmetric. Define indecomposable by absence of a nontrivial block partition.

items.title: Symmetrizable generalized cartan matrix
items.statement: Definition: $A$ is symmetrisable if $DA$ is symmetric for a positive diagonal $D$.
items.strategy: Fix positive rational d_i with d_i a_ij=d_j a_ji, scaling to integers componentwise if desired. Prove rational normalization by propagating the positive ratios along a finite spanning tree; cycle consistency follows from the supplied symmetrizer. Translate Kleshchev A=diag(epsilon_i)B by d_i=1/epsilon_i, not by d_i=epsilon_i.

items.title: Realization of a generalized cartan matrix
items.statement: Definition: a realisation $(\mathfrak h,\Pi,\Pi^\vee)$ has linearly independent simple roots/coroots and $\alpha_j(h_i)=a_{ij}$, with minimal dimension $2n-\operatorname{rank}A$.
items.strategy: Work over C; h_i and alpha_i are each independent, alpha_j(h_i)=a_ij and dim h=2n-rank A. An isomorphism preserves both indexed families; it need not be unique.
source_locators: Kleshchev Definition 1.2.2, pp.10--11; Perrin Definition 4.1.1, p.29

items.title: Minimal realizations exist and are unique up to isomorphism
items.statement: Proposition: every GCM has a minimal realisation, unique by an isomorphism respecting root/coroot data.
items.strategy: Use the rank-r pairing of the coroot span with the simple-root span. Extend its row and column spaces separately to obtain independent roots and coroots on a (2n-r)-space; use independent row/column rank pivots, not the unjustified assertion that a general nonsymmetric A has a nonsingular principal rank minor. For uniqueness compare kernels of the map h -> C^n, choose finite complements, and change complementary coordinates by the coroot span. The resulting linear isomorphism preserves both families. Finite linear elimination adds no AC.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 1.2.4, pp.11--12; Perrin Proposition 4.1.2, pp.29--30

items.title: Kac Moody root lattice height and positive cone
items.statement: Q is the free abelian span of the independent alpha_i; Qplus is their nonnegative span, ht(sum k_i alpha_i)=sum k_i, and mu<=lambda means lambda-mu in Qplus.
items.strategy: Specify Qplus contains zero; roots themselves exclude zero. The simple-root independence makes both coordinates and the height unambiguous.

items.title: PBW for countably presented Kac Moody Lie algebras
items.statement: For a complex Lie algebra with a supplied countable ordered basis, finite ordered monomials form a basis of its tensor-quotient enveloping algebra. In the finite-word graded algebras used here compatible bases of graded subalgebras and quotients can be selected without AC.
items.strategy: Repeat the terminating reduction x_j x_i -> x_i x_j+[x_j,x_i] on finite words, ordered by length and inversion count. Prove confluence by induction on this measure: disjoint reductions commute; the triple overlap reduces to Jacobi; bilinearity preserves finite sums. A finite ordered normal form kills each defining relation in every word context, so it factors through the quotient and is inverse to the ordered-word map. No bound on the number of available basis elements is used. For each finite graded component enumerate bracket words lexicographically and retain the first independent images; finite row reduction gives compatible bases of kernels. For an arbitrary countably spanned algebra choose successive independent vectors from its given enumeration. State no arbitrary unbased PBW assertion.

items.title: Free Lie construction for finite Kac Moody generators
items.statement: The free Lie algebra on a finite-dimensional complex space is the formal bracket-word quotient by bilinearity, antisymmetry and Jacobi; it embeds into its tensor algebra and its enveloping algebra is that tensor algebra.
items.strategy: First construct the abstract bracket-word quotient, which has the universal property by recursive evaluation and is countably spanned. The universal properties give inverse associative maps between its enveloping algebra and the tensor algebra. PBW injectivity embeds the abstract free Lie algebra into the tensor algebra; its image is the Lie subalgebra generated by the letters. This avoids assuming freeness from a concrete subalgebra before its universal property is proved.

items.title: Contragredient lie algebra before the maximal ideal quotient
items.statement: Definition: $\widetilde{\mathfrak g}(A)$ is generated by $\mathfrak h,e_i,f_i$ with Cartan and $[e_i,f_j]=\delta_{ij}h_i$ relations.
items.strategy: Take the free Lie algebra on a fixed finite basis of h and e_i,f_i, quotient by [h,hprime]=0, [h,e_i]=alpha_i(h)e_i, [h,f_i]=-alpha_i(h)f_i, [e_i,f_j]=delta_ij h_i. State the quotient universal property. Cartan injectivity and freeness of the halves are obligations supplied next, not assumptions.

items.title: Contragredient algebra has a triangular decomposition
items.statement: Proposition: $\widetilde{\mathfrak g}=\widetilde{\mathfrak n}^-\oplus\mathfrak h\oplus\widetilde{\mathfrak n}^+$ and is root-graded.
items.strategy: Use T(C^n) with f_i acting by left concatenation; h on a word has eigenvalue lambda minus its root sum; recursively e_i(f_j a)=delta_ij h_i(a)+f_j e_i(a). Check all four relation families by word-length induction. Evaluation on 1 for every lambda proves Cartan injectivity and independence of the negative half; the involution e_i -> -f_i, f_i -> -e_i, h -> -h supplies the other half. Reordering mixed brackets by Jacobi proves spanning. The embedding of each free half into its tensor algebra proves freeness. State the Q-grading and the finite word bound at each height.
source_locators: Kleshchev Theorem 1.3.3, pp.13--16; Perrin Theorem 4.1.6, pp.30--33

items.title: The sum of triangularly disjoint graded ideals is disjoint from h
items.statement: Lemma: ideals meeting $\mathfrak h$ trivially are closed under sums and their sum remains disjoint from $\mathfrak h$.
items.strategy: For any ideal and each vector with finite weight support, choose h separating those finitely many weights and apply Lagrange interpolation polynomials in ad h to extract every component. Thus every ideal is graded, not merely ideals declared graded. The zero component of every ideal disjoint from h is zero, and remains zero in their arbitrary algebraic sum. Show the positive and negative intersections are separate ideals using [f_i,nplus] subset nplus+h and zero Cartan intersection. This constructs the largest ideal r without Zorn or AC.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 1.3.2 and Theorem 1.3.3, pp.13--16; Perrin Theorem 4.1.6(v), pp.30--33

items.title: Kac moody algebra associated to a gcm
items.statement: Definition: $\mathfrak g(A)=\widetilde{\mathfrak g}(A)/\mathfrak r$, where $\mathfrak r$ is the maximal graded ideal meeting $\mathfrak h$ trivially.
items.strategy: Define g(A)=gtilde/r using the proved largest ideal. Transport h, e_i, f_i and the sign-changing involution. Any nonzero ideal of g has nonzero intersection with h, by taking its inverse image; do not confuse this property with simplicity.

items.title: Kac moody root spaces are finite dimensional
items.statement: Proposition: $\mathfrak g(A)=\mathfrak h\oplus\bigoplus_{\alpha\in\Delta}\mathfrak g_\alpha$ with finite-dimensional nonzero root spaces.
items.strategy: Quotient the homogeneous decomposition. At height m the half is spanned by finitely many iterated brackets in n generators; dim g_alpha <= n^m. The only pure simple-root degrees are plus/minus alpha_i, each one-dimensional, because [e_i,e_i]=0 and h_i=[e_i,f_i] is nonzero. Every nonzero root has one sign. Include that a simple reflection can change a positive root to negative only for alpha_i once its image is known to be a root.
source_locators: Kleshchev Theorem 1.3.3 and §1.4, pp.13--19; Perrin Theorem 4.1.6 and Definitions 4.1.8--4.1.9, pp.30--34

items.title: The opposite simple centralizer in a Kac Moody half vanishes
items.statement: An element of nplus commuting with every f_i is zero; likewise nminus and e_i.
items.strategy: Use finite weight interpolation to reduce to a weight component. Its span under iterated ad h and ad e_i stays in nplus and is stable under every ad f_i by Jacobi and the defining relations. It is therefore an ideal disjoint from h and vanishes by maximality. Apply the sign-changing involution for the other half.

items.title: Serre elements vanish before Serre generation
items.statement: For every GCM, (ad e_i)^(1-a_ij)e_j and its negative analogue vanish in the maximal-ideal quotient.
items.strategy: Derive [e,f^m]=m f^(m-1)(h-m+1) by induction. Apply to v=f_j of i-weight -a_ij. The putative Serre vector is killed by e_i, by every e_k outside i,j, and by e_j using a_ij=0 iff a_ji=0 in the boundary case. The opposite-simple-centralizer lemma kills it. This proves vanishing only; generation waits for the Casimir relation-module proof.

items.title: Simple reflections and the kac moody weyl group
items.statement: Definition: $s_i(\lambda)=\lambda-\lambda(h_i)\alpha_i$ and $W=\langle s_i\rangle$.
items.strategy: Define s_i(lambda)=lambda-lambda(h_i)alpha_i and W as their subgroup in GL(hstar); compute s_i^2=1 and the dual action s_i(h)=h-alpha_i(h)h_i. This definition precedes use of W in the residual-kernel proof.

items.title: The weyl group preserves roots and root multiplicities
items.statement: Proposition: $W$ permutes $\Delta$ and preserves $\dim\mathfrak g_\alpha$.
items.strategy: For any GCM (no symmetrizability required), use Serre vanishing and the binomial derivation identity to construct the finite adjoint exponentials. Compute their action on h_i,e_i,f_i and on ker alpha_i in h; they send g_alpha bijectively to g_s_i(alpha), so multiplicity and roots are preserved. In the symmetrizable case compute form preservation directly from the reflection formula.

items.title: Invariant bilinear form for a symmetrizable kac moody algebra
items.statement: Theorem: a symmetrisable $\mathfrak g(A)$ has the standard nondegenerate invariant form after the necessary Cartan extension.
items.strategy: Normalize (h_i,h)=alpha_i(h)/d_i and (e_i,f_j)=delta_ij/d_i. Fix a finite complement to the coroot span and set its self-pairing zero. Prove nondegeneracy on h: the annihilator of all simple roots lies in the coroot span, whose radical has dimension n-r; then root independence kills a vector in the full radical. Extend the form by height, setting unequal opposite degrees orthogonal and (x,[u,v])=([x,u],v). Prove independence of both bracket expressions using the four-term Jacobi calculation of Kleshchev Theorem 2.2.3 and check invariance also in degrees N,-N,0. The radical is a graded ideal disjoint from h, hence zero. Conclude perfect opposite-root pairings, (alpha_i,alpha_j)=d_i a_ij, and [x_alpha,y_minusalpha]=(x,y)nu^{-1}(alpha). This proof precedes Serre generation.

items.title: Kac moody category o
items.statement: Definition: weight modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces and support in finitely many downward cones form the Kac--Moody version of $\mathcal O$.
items.strategy: Define weight modules with finite-dimensional weight spaces and support in finitely many sets lambda-Qplus; morphisms preserve the action. No finite generation or finite length is imposed. Finite positive-root degrees above a fixed weight imply restrictedness: if mu+beta<=lambda_j then beta has bounded nonnegative coordinates. Submodules and quotients inherit weight decompositions by finite interpolation.

items.title: Kac moody verma module
items.statement: Definition: $M_A(\lambda)=U\mathfrak g(A)\otimes_{U\mathfrak b}\mathbb C_\lambda$.
items.strategy: Define b=h+nplus and M_A(lambda)=U(g) tensor over U(b) C_lambda, with nplus killing 1. The countable PBW lemma gives M as U(nminus) with a one-dimensional top and finite lower weight spaces. Include the unquotiented Mtilde used later. This is independent of the finite-dimensional published Verma theorem. Category O membership is asserted for M_A only; Mtilde is a module for the universal algebra with analogous weight finiteness, without an asserted quotient action.

items.title: Generalized casimir on restricted kac moody modules
items.statement: Define restricted modules, choose $\rho(h_i)=1$, and define the Cartan term plus the root-degree dual-basis sum $\Omega$.
items.strategy: Restricted means g_alpha v=0 for all but finitely many positive roots for each v. Fix rho(h_i)=1. With dual Cartan bases u_a,u^a and opposite-root dual bases x_alpha,s and y_alpha,s, define Omega=2nu^{-1}(rho)+sum u_a u^a+2sum y_alpha,s x_alpha,s as an operator on restricted modules. The last sum is pointwise finite; each finite-dimensional canonical tensor is basis independent. No infinite element of U(g) is asserted.

items.title: Generalized kac moody casimir is central and scalar on highest weight modules
items.statement: Prove the dual-basis commutator cancellation, centrality of $\Omega$, and its scalar $(\lambda+2\rho\mid\lambda)$ on a module generated by a highest-weight vector.
items.strategy: Pair the tensor identity sum y_alpha tensor [z,x_alpha]=sum [y_beta,z] tensor x_beta against each opposite tensor factor; invariance proves equality. For z=e_i telescope the two root-index sums in [Omega_0,z], leaving only the simple-root boundary; check z=f_i likewise and Cartan commutators directly. The boundary cancels the commutator of the finite Cartan term and 2nu^{-1}(rho). On a highest vector the positive factors vanish and the remaining scalar is (lambda+2rho,lambda); centrality propagates it to the generated module. No Serre or later representation theorem enters.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 2.3.1, Theorem 2.3.5 and Corollary 2.3.6, pp.32--36

items.title: Bounded above kac moody weight modules are generated by primitive vectors
items.statement: Define a primitive vector as a highest-weight vector modulo a submodule. Prove that an object of $\mathcal O$ is generated by primitive vectors under $U(\mathfrak n^-)$.
items.strategy: A nonzero weight vector is primitive if its class is a nonzero highest vector modulo some submodule. It fails to be primitive precisely when it belongs to U(g)nplus v=U(nminus)U_0(nplus)v; prove this equality by PBW, including Cartan weights. In that event it is a finite sum of negative words applied to higher weight vectors. Induct on the finite set of support weights above the given weight to show that every vector is in the nminus-span of primitive vectors. No finite composition series is claimed.

items.title: Enveloping quotient kernels and augmentation intersections
items.statement: For a Lie quotient prove $\ker U(\theta)=\mathfrak r U(\mathfrak g)$; for a subalgebra prove $\mathfrak r\cap\mathfrak r U_0(\mathfrak g)=[\mathfrak r,\mathfrak r]$.
items.strategy: For countably spanned complex Lie algebras with supplied compatible ordered bases, first prove ker(U(g)->U(g/r))=rU(g) when r is an ideal, by inverse universal-property maps. For any Lie algebra l in this class, prove l intersect U_0(l)^2=[l,l]: one inclusion is xy-yx=[x,y], and the reverse follows by mapping to U(l/[l,l]), the symmetric algebra where degree-one and degree-at-least-two parts are disjoint. For a subalgebra r of g, order a basis of r before its complement. Let W be the vector span of the nonempty ordered monomials in the complement. PBW gives U(g)=U(r) direct-sum (U(r) tensor W) as a left U(r)-module, and U_0(g)=U_0(r) direct-sum (U(r) tensor W). Multiplying on the left by r gives rU_0(g)=U_0(r)^2 direct-sum (U_0(r) tensor W), because rU(r)=U_0(r) and rU_0(r)=U_0(r)^2 (both follow by expanding nonempty words in generators). Intersect with r, which lies in the first PBW summand, to obtain r intersect rU_0(g)=r intersect U_0(r)^2=[r,r]. Do not assert that ordered monomials of length at least two alone span rU_0(g): commutators can contribute degree-one basis vectors. For the finite-word graded applications choose compatible bases degree by degree by finite elimination; no unbased infinite-dimensional choice assertion is used.

items.title: Kac moody relation module embeds in verma modules and obeys the casimir constraint
items.statement: Construct $\mathfrak r^-/[\mathfrak r^-,\mathfrak r^-]\hookrightarrow\bigoplus_i M(-\alpha_i)$ using the free contragredient negative half. Prove injectivity with the augmentation lemma; primitive generation and Casimir imply that ideal generators have $(\alpha\mid\alpha)=2(\rho\mid\alpha)$.
items.strategy: Use the last-letter decomposition T(f_i)=C1 plus direct sum T(f_i)f_i, identifying Mtilde(0)prime with direct sum Mtilde(-alpha_i). After quotienting by r, identify the induced module with direct sum M(-alpha_i). The map a -> 1 tensor a v factors through rminus/[rminus,rminus]; use ASSOCIATIVE last-letter coefficients, not adjoint coefficients, to prove its kernel is rminus intersect rminus U_0(ntilde_minus)=[rminus,rminus]. Each summand has Casimir scalar zero since (alpha_i,alpha_i)=2(rho,alpha_i). Primitive generation gives relation generators in degrees alpha not simple satisfying (alpha,alpha)=2(rho,alpha). Lift from the abelianization by minimum-height induction: a nonzero positively graded quotient cannot equal its own commutator algebra. Check the actions explicitly before invoking the scalar.

items.title: The serre quotient has weyl symmetry and no residual kac moody kernel
items.statement: First prove that Serre elements vanish in the maximal-ideal quotient, using adjoint rank-one calculations and the no-commuting-vector consequence of maximality. On the quotient by Serre elements, prove local nilpotence and use finite exponential operators for Weyl symmetry. A minimum-height residual-kernel weight contradicts the preceding Casimir constraint.
items.strategy: The Serre-vanishing lemma gives gbar->g. Serre relations imply ad e_i and ad f_i are locally nilpotent on every generator of gbar; the binomial derivation formula propagates this to all bracket words. Finite exponentials exp(ad f_i)exp(-ad e_i)exp(ad f_i) are automorphisms inducing s_i on h, both on gbar and g. They preserve kernel root multiplicities. If its positive part is nonzero take minimum height alpha; the generator constraint forces (alpha,alpha)=2(rho,alpha)>0. Since alpha is not simple, s_i alpha remains positive and minimality forces alpha(h_i)<=0 for every i; thus (alpha,alpha)=sum k_i d_i alpha(h_i)<=0. Contradiction. This Weyl argument does not use identification of the two quotients.
source_locators: Kleshchev Lemma 3.1.1, §3.2 and Theorem 9.3.5 proof, pp.37--42, 125--126

items.title: Serre presentation of a kac moody algebra
items.statement: Theorem: for symmetrizable $A$, the ideals $\mathfrak r\cap\widetilde{\mathfrak n}^{\pm}$ are generated by the corresponding Serre elements, so $\mathfrak g(A)$ has the Chevalley--Serre presentation.
items.strategy: Apply the preceding zero-residual-kernel lemma to both halves, using the sign-changing involution for the negative half. State precisely symmetrizable finite GCM over C; rplus and rminus are generated by their corresponding Serre elements. Triangular decomposition of the quotient and the PBW multiplication isomorphism then follow from the earlier Lie decomposition and the countable PBW lemma.

items.title: Real and imaginary kac moody roots
items.statement: Definition: real roots are $W\Pi$; all other roots are imaginary, with positive/negative sign inherited from $Q^+$.
items.strategy: Define Delta_real=W Pi and Delta_imag=Delta minus Delta_real; retain positive and negative signs from the root lattice. The terms do not mean positive and negative squared length unless symmetrizability and the corresponding theorem have been proved.

items.title: Real root spaces are one dimensional sl2 roots
items.statement: Proposition: each real root has multiplicity one and an associated $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ triple.
items.strategy: Transport the simple triple (e_i,h_i,f_i) by a product of the proved automorphisms. It spans a copy of sl2 in degrees alpha,0,-alpha. Transporting the simple root space shows its dimension is one and no other nonzero scalar multiple of alpha is a root except +/-alpha. If the real coroot is named, check independence of the transporter by transporting [g_alpha,g_minusalpha] and imposing alpha(h_alpha)=2.

items.title: Strict linear alternative for GCM trichotomy
items.statement: For finitely many real row vectors v_i, there is x with v_i x>0 for every i iff no nonzero nonnegative linear combination of the v_i is zero. Consequently if u>=0 and C^t u>=0 imply u=0, there is v>0 with Cv<0.
items.strategy: Minimize the squared Euclidean norm on the finite convex hull. It is closed and bounded (derive compactness from the finite simplex and its continuous linear image); the hypothesis excludes zero. For a minimum x, expand ||x+t(y-x)||^2 and divide by t>0 to get (x,y)>=||x||^2>0. The reverse implication follows by pairing with x. Apply to rows of -C and standard coordinate rows for the consequence. This external compactness supplier needs its transitive proof audit before readiness.

items.title: Finite affine indefinite trichotomy for indecomposable gcms
items.statement: Theorem (over real vectors): for an indecomposable GCM A exactly one of the following mutually exclusive clauses holds, and this clause defines its type. Finite type: det A is nonzero, some u>0 has Au>0, and Au>=0 implies u>0 or u=0. Affine type: corank A=1, some u>0 has Au=0, and Au>=0 implies Au=0; equivalently K_A={x:Ax>=0}=ker A=Ru, so the positive null ray is unique. Indefinite type: some u>0 has Au<0, and x>=0 and Ax>=0 imply x=0. A and A^t have the same type. Finite- and affine-type GCMs are symmetrisable. If A is symmetrisable and B=DA is its symmetric positive-diagonal symmetrisation, then finite type is equivalent to B positive definite, affine type to B positive semidefinite of corank one with kernel Ru, and indefinite type to B indefinite.
items.strategy: Prove the full positive-vector trichotomy for every indecomposable GCM, not only symmetrizable matrices: exactly one of Au>0, Au=0, Au<0 has a solution u>0. Include the corresponding cone conditions, corank one and uniqueness in the affine case, and transpose invariance. Follow Kleshchev 4.1.6--4.1.12: zero-coordinate propagation; split K_A={u:Au>=0} into the strictly positive cone or one-dimensional null-line cases; perturb the zero coordinates of Au to strict positivity; use the strict linear alternative for the empty nonnegative-cone case. For symmetrizable A and a positive trichotomy vector u use the directly expanded identity x^t DA x = sum_i d_i(Au)_i x_i^2/u_i + sum_{i<j}(-d_i a_ij)u_i u_j(x_i/u_i-x_j/u_j)^2. In finite type it is positive definite. In affine type it is positive semidefinite with kernel Ru by connectedness. In indefinite type u has negative quadratic value whereas coordinate vectors have positive value. The converse follows from the already proved trichotomy. No spectral theorem is used. Finite/affine symmetrizability requires the additional cycle argument of 4.2.2--4.2.3; include it inline rather than infer it from terminology.

items.title: Finite-type Kac–Moody roots descend to simple roots
items.statement: For a finite-type GCM A, every root of g(A) is Weyl-conjugate to a simple root, and there are finitely many roots. Every root space has dimension one, and g(A) is finite-dimensional.
items.strategy: Work componentwise with the positive definite symmetrization B=DA proved by the local trichotomy, using (alpha_i,alpha_j)=d_i a_ij. For a positive root beta=sum m_i alpha_i, positivity of (beta,beta)=sum m_i(alpha_i,beta) gives i with (alpha_i,beta)>0. Thus beta(h_i)>0 is an integer. If beta is not simple, its support contains an index different from i: the local root-space result excludes pure multiples k alpha_i with k>1. The reflected root s_i beta=beta-beta(h_i)alpha_i retains a positive coefficient at that different index. The proved one-sign root decomposition and Weyl root invariance therefore make it positive, and its height is smaller. Induction on the positive integer height reaches a simple root. Negative roots follow by sign and the simple reflection of alpha_i to -alpha_i. Weyl form invariance implies every root has squared length in the finite set {2d_i}. To prove finiteness without a compact-orthogonal-group theorem, let v_i be the basis dual to the alpha_i for the positive form. Cauchy–Schwarz follows directly by minimizing (u-t v,u-t v) over real t. Hence each integer root coefficient satisfies |m_i|^2=|(beta,v_i)|^2<=C(v_i,v_i), where C=max_i 2d_i. Only finitely many integer coefficient tuples meet these finitely many fixed bounds. Existence of the dual basis follows by finite Gaussian elimination since positivity makes B invertible. Weyl transport preserves the one-dimensional simple root spaces. Finally the existing triangular weight decomposition is h plus the root spaces, and dim h=n because A is invertible. Thus dim g=n+|Delta| is finite. No classification, root-string completeness, highest-root theorem, recurrence or external Serre existence theorem is assumed.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 4.3.2, printed pp.63–64, complete proof read; local height descent and dual-basis lattice bound replace its compact-group route

references.title: Kleshchev Proposition 4.3.2, printed pp.63–64, complete proof read; local height descent and dual-basis lattice bound replace its compact-group route

items.title: Nonsingular indecomposable Kac–Moody algebras are simple
items.statement: If A is an indecomposable GCM with det A nonzero, then g(A) is nonabelian and has no nonzero proper Lie ideal. In particular every indecomposable finite-type component is simple. A Lie ideal means a linear subspace J with [g,J] contained in J; simple here means nonabelian with no nonzero proper ideal.
items.strategy: By the maximal-ideal quotient construction, every nonzero ideal J of g intersects h nontrivially: its inverse image would otherwise be an ideal disjoint from h larger than the defining maximal one. Let 0!=h in J intersect h. Since A is nonsingular, the n independent simple roots form a basis of h-star (dim h=n), so alpha_i(h)!=0 for some i. Then [h,e_i]=alpha_i(h)e_i puts e_i in J, [e_i,f_i]=h_i puts h_i in J, and [h_i,f_i]=-2f_i puts f_i in J. If a_ij!=0, [h_i,e_j]=a_ij e_j puts e_j in J, hence also h_j and f_j. The graph whose edges are nonzero off-diagonal entries is connected by indecomposability, so a finite path repeats this argument at every index. The h_i span h because A is nonsingular. All defining generators lie in J, so J=g. The simple sl2 triple is nonzero by Cartan injectivity and the root-space construction, showing g is nonabelian. This proves simplicity directly rather than invoking a classification or a radical theorem.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 1.4.8(i), printed pp.19–20, complete simplicity argument read

references.title: Kleshchev Proposition 1.4.8(i), printed pp.19–20, complete simplicity argument read

items.title: Finite type kac moody algebras recover the dg semisimple algebras
items.statement: For a finite-type Cartan matrix A over C, g(A) is finite-dimensional and is a direct sum of nonabelian simple Lie algebras, one for each indecomposable component (thus semisimple). Its simple-root/coroot pairing is A, with rows indexing coroots. Intrinsically, g(A) is the universal complex Lie algebra on its minimal-realisation Cartan space and Chevalley generators, subject to [h,h']=0, [h,e_i]=alpha_i(h)e_i, [h,f_i]=-alpha_i(h)f_i, [e_i,f_j]=delta_ij h_i, and (ad e_i)^(1-a_ij)e_j=(ad f_i)^(1-a_ij)f_j=0 for i not equal to j; no finite-Dynkin classification theorem is assumed.
items.strategy: The local finite-type trichotomy gives symmetrizability, a positive definite symmetrization and rank A=n, hence h=span(h_i). The root-descent lemma proves finite dimension. For each indecomposable component the simplicity lemma proves the associated algebra is nonabelian simple. For different components the Cartan relations and zero-entry Serre relations give zero brackets for every pair of generators (e_i,e_j), (f_i,f_j), (e_i,f_j) and (h_i,h_j), as well as the mixed Cartan-root brackets. Jacobi then makes the generated component subalgebras commute. The local symmetrizable Serre theorem identifies g(A) with the universal algebra of precisely these intrinsic Cartan and both Serre relation families. Mapping each generator into its component gives a homomorphism to the direct sum of the component presentations, and inclusions of the component generators give the reverse homomorphism. Their composites fix all generators, hence are identities. This proves the direct-sum assertion, not merely a quotient of a direct sum. The existing root decomposition, one-sign property and root descent identify the simple roots and their matrix alpha_j(h_i)=a_ij. No external finite-type presentation or classification theorem is used. The statements of simplicity and semisimplicity are explicit above, so no unprovided radical criterion is used.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 1.4.8(i), pp.19–20; Proposition 4.3.2, pp.63–64; complete proofs read, local height/lattice proof supplies finite dimension

title: Kac Moody Algebras from Generalized Cartan Matrices — Examples

items.title: Rank one gcm recovers sl2
items.statement: Example: $A=(2)$ gives $\mathfrak{sl}_2$.
items.strategy: For A=(2), no off-diagonal Serre relations exist. All brackets reduce to span e,f,h; E12,E21,diag(1,-1) give independent matrix images and all three sl2 brackets. Thus the universal algebra is exactly sl2.

items.title: The a2 serre relations
items.statement: Example: write the two quadratic Serre relations and recover the finite roots.
items.strategy: For A2 write (ad e1)^2 e2=(ad e2)^2 e1=0 and both negative analogues. The positive half is spanned by e1,e2,[e1,e2], with independence witnessed by E12,E23,E13. Opposite matrices and diagonal coroots give the eight-dimensional sl3 model; verify the six nonzero roots and the row/coroot convention.

items.title: The affine a1 gcm has singular rank one realization data
items.statement: Example: $\begin{psmallmatrix}2&-2\\-2&2\end{psmallmatrix}$ requires a Cartan of dimension three.
items.strategy: For [[2,-2],[-2,2]], n=2 and rank=1, hence dim h=3. Choose independent h0,h1,d and define alpha0=(2,-2,1), alpha1=(-2,2,0) in their dual coordinates. Verify independence and all four Cartan pairings; h0+h1 is killed by both roots.

items.title: A symmetrizable indefinite rank two gcm
items.statement: Example: $\begin{psmallmatrix}2&-3\\-3&2\end{psmallmatrix}$ has imaginary roots.
items.strategy: For [[2,-3],[-3,2]], d1=d2=1, det=-5 and A(1,1)^t=(-1,-1)^t. The positive Lie degree (1,1) survives the Serre quotient because defining positive Serre generators have total degree 5; its nonzero bracket [e1,e2] has root alpha1+alpha2 of squared norm -2. All real roots have positive norm by form-preserving Weyl transport, so it is imaginary.
source_locators: Kleshchev §4.1, pp.50--57 and Theorem 9.3.5, pp.125--126; explicit degree-(1,1) computation supplied locally

items.title: A matrix with one zero off diagonal is not a gcm
items.statement: Counterexample violating $a_{ij}=0\Leftrightarrow a_{ji}=0$.
items.strategy: Use [[2,0],[-1,2]]. Its diagonal and nonpositive integral off-diagonal conditions hold, but a12=0 and a21=-1 violate the symmetric zero condition. It is not a GCM.
source_locators: Finite matrix check; no dependency may cite this row

items.title: Imaginary root spaces need not have multiplicity one
items.statement: Counterexample in affine type: multiples of $\delta$ have rank-sized multiplicity.
items.strategy: Use untwisted affine A2: all diagonal entries 2 and all off-diagonal entries -1. Give a self-contained loop-sl3 model C[t,t^-1] tensor sl3 plus Cc+Cd with central term m delta_m,-n tr(xy) and degree derivation. Check Jacobi by invariance of trace and m+n+k=0; take e0=tE31,e1=E12,e2=E23, opposite f0=t^-1 E13,f1=E21,f2=E32 and h0=c-E11+E33. Check generation using matrix commutators. The Cartan has dimension 4; each real root space is C t^m Eij and each m delta space (m!=0) is t^m times the two-dimensional traceless diagonal space. A nonzero ideal disjoint from Cartan has a homogeneous nonzero vector; bracket with the opposite matrix unit, or pair a nonzero diagonal against a diagonal using trace at degree -m, to obtain a nonzero Cartan element. Thus the model is the maximal-ideal quotient by the same recognition argument as Kleshchev 1.5.1. Since delta has norm zero, these are imaginary roots of multiplicity 2, for every nonzero m. This explicit verification avoids a forbidden forward dependency on RL-13.
source_locators: Kleshchev Proposition 1.5.1, Lemma 1.5.3 and Example 1.5.4, pp.20--25; local adaptation to the sl3 loop model
